description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

chronologies.date: “it happened that the Olympic festival fell exactly at this same period”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 7.206 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 506 (PDF p. 508)
chronologies.note: The allies send only an advance guard to Thermopylae because of the Carneian and Olympic festivals. Agrees with CFAH: AP-13 puts the invasion 296 years after the First Olympiad (AP-10, 776/775 BC), and 296 = 74 × 4, so 480 BC is an Olympic year.

chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 8.26 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 528 (PDF p. 530)
chronologies.note: Arcadian deserters to Xerxes, after Thermopylae. Same Olympic year as 7.206.
